page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor, it features 16 physical cores configured with hyperthreading to deliver 32 dedicated vCPUs. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache, supporting AVX and AVX-512 foundation instruction sets. Memory capacity is configured at 64 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2 GB per core. The server includes no integrated GPU accelerators and offers no local disk storage, while providing a network baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reveal clear distinctions between single-thread and multi-core throughput. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, score in lower tiers due to the processor generation and clock rate. Conversely, parallel execution scales adequately into average benchmark tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8384.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 23528.93. The instance demonstrates steady mid-tier capability across Clang software compilation, ray tracing, Redis SET operations at 23.22 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaching 13.98 GB/sec.

Resource efficiency is centered on high core density for multi-threaded processes rather than high per-thread burst speeds. A key operational tradeoff is the absence of local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached block volumes for persistence. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compute workloads, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed backend microservices, background job queues, and static web hosting where individual thread performance is secondary to aggregate thread capacity.

The instance includes no bundled local storage and features no hardware GPU accelerators, utilizing remote block storage and relying on a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. Benchmark evaluations show modest single-core throughput, reflected in lower-tier Geekbench and stress-ng single-threaded results, while multi-core performance scales into average tiers for parallel execution such as Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving. Qualitative cost efficiency centers on multi-threaded compute density rather than single-threaded speed or high-speed local IOPS. This profile fits distributed microservices, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, batch computing, and mid-tier web serving workloads that do not require low single-core latency or onboard disk storage.
